newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bordeaux air cargo traffic down 4 pct in Jan-Oct.
newsitem.headline: Bordeaux air cargo traffic down 4 pct in Jan-Oct.

text.p: Bordeaux's Merignac airport handled 6,408 tonnes of air cargo in the first ten months of 1996, down four percent on the same period last year.
In October 1996, United Parcel Service, launched a weekday feeder service between Lyon-Satolas airport and Bordeaux using two-tonne capacity Beechcraft 1900 aircraft.
Bordeaux also features on DHL Worldwide Express's Brussels-western France service in a Brussels-Nantes-Bordeaux routing using a 6.5 tonnes-capacity Convair aircraft.
Airfreight is also carried in the bellyholds of passenger aircraft operating domestic, European and long-haul services from Bordeaux.

Since the beginning of last month, French airline, Air Liberte has withdrawn its twice-weekly Airbus 310-200 passenger frequencies between Bordeaux and Abidjan, which had offered four to five tonnes of freight capacity per flight
Several airlines also operate trucking services for airfreight from Bordeaux.
Jan-Oct 1996 postal traffic at Bordeaux totalled 10,794 tonnes, or 20 percent above 1995 levels.

French airline, L'Aeropostale, carries overnight mail between its Paris-Charles de Gaulle hub and Bordeaux on a regular basis using a Boeing 737QC aircraft. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
